title: The Instruction Tax on Factual Recall: Base Models Can Beat Their Instruction-Tuned Counterparts
abstract: arXiv:2610.28407v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We present our solution to the AKBC LM-KBC 2026 Shared Task, where we achieved a score of 0.6836 on the official leaderboard, more than double the baseline of 0.2964. This task requires generating all possible objects for subject-relation pairs using a language model with up to 32 billion parameters, with no retrieval or fine-tuning involved. We show that the prompting methodology is as important as the model architecture: while the instruction-tuned model version achieves 0.5681 with its chat interface, the base model achieves 0.6836 when prompted using text completion. Thus, instruction tuning decreases factual recall; we refer to this effect as the instruction tax, which is caused by the model's weights rather than the prompting method. Our final solution is fairly straightforward: we prompt the base model with some examples from the training data, generate 64--256 outputs, and retain only the repeated ones. Two specialized methods

translated_title: 事实回忆中的指令税：基础模型可以胜过其指令微调版本
translated_abstract: 我们展示了针对AKBC LM-KBC 2026共享任务的解决方案，在官方排行榜上取得了0.6836的分数，是0.2964基线的两倍多。该任务要求使用参数量不超过320亿的语言模型，在不进行检索或微调的情况下，为主体-关系对生成所有可能的宾语对象。我们表明，提示方法与模型架构同样重要：指令微调版本的模型通过其聊天界面只能达到0.5681，而基础模型在使用文本补全提示时能达到0.6836。因此，指令微调会降低事实回忆能力；我们将这一效应称为“指令税”，它由模型的权重本身导致，而非提示方法所致。我们的最终解决方案相当简单直接：用训练数据中的一些示例提示基础模型，生成64至256个输出，并只保留其中重复出现的内容，此外还使用了两种专门的方法。
tldr: 该论文发现指令微调会降低语言模型的事实回忆能力（即“指令税”），通过简单的文本补全方式提示基础模型并仅保留重复输出，在AKBC LM-KBC 2026共享任务上取得了超过基线两倍的0.6836分。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals an "instruction tax" — instruction tuning degrades factual recall in language models — and achieves 0.6836 on the AKBC LM-KBC 2026 shared task (more than double the baseline) by simply prompting the base model via text completion and keeping only repeated outputs.
